title: MistyJungleFlip against itself: the turn-overs decide it
intro: MistyJungleFlip against itself at 7.5 million nodes a move, three times the strength the site's bot plays at, read again by the same engine at the same depth. Marks (?!, ?, ??) grade each move against its choice; none was needed, because no move cost its player more than a few points. The graph is Red's chance as the engine saw it, and the die beside a turned-over tile grades how lucky the turn was from what both players could see. The game is won in the first five turn-overs.

comments.2: Blue's first tile is a dog, beside Red's rat, which it can now take. Red's chance drops to about four in ten.
comments.3: The luck of the game. Red turns up its elephant, the strongest piece, and its chance jumps from about four in ten to three in four.
comments.5: And again: a red tiger next to Blue's dog. Red is now near nine in ten, from two turn-overs that any other tile could have spoiled.
comments.11: And the wolf. Blue has turned over four pieces and lost two of them.
comments.18: Blue's lion takes the dog back.
comments.24: Blue turns up its elephant at last. The engine slightly preferred moving the tiger to d2 first, but the turn-over cost only a couple of points, not enough for a mark.
comments.30: Blue turns over Red's leopard, a gamble that was right on average and comes up badly: the leopard takes Blue's rat next move, and Red's chance is 97 in 100 from here.
comments.47: The rat takes Blue's elephant, the one capture only a rat can make.
comments.55: Red's lion takes Blue's last piece, its lion. Blue has no move, and Red wins.
